transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been concerning you?

Hi, nice to meet you. Um, I came in because... well, I just feel like I’m crawling out of my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. It happens a lot in the radiology suite, or when I'm in my classes. I've been trying to just tough it out for months now, but it's not working. I always end up pacing, or constantly shifting around, or just finding some excuse so I can get up and move.
When you're in class or in the radiology suite and you're feeling that need to move around, are you also having trouble focusing on what's being taught or what you're supposed to be doing?

Not really, no. I mean, I don't think I have a problem focusing. I usually know exactly what's going on in the lecture, or what I'm supposed to be doing with the equipment. It's just... I physically can't stay still while I'm doing it. So, yeah, my attention seems fine, it's really just that intense need to keep moving.

When you feel that need to move around, does it feel like there's an uncomfortable tension or restless feeling inside your body that gets better when you move, or is it more just that your body wants to be in motion?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about it like that. Um, I don't know if it's a specific tension inside or if my body just wants to be moving... I just know that sitting still feels impossible. 

Like, I physically just have to be doing something. So I guess I don't really have a good answer for exactly what it feels like, just that moving is the only thing that makes it go away.
How long have you been experiencing this need to move around and inability to sit still? Has this been something you've dealt with your whole life, or did it start more recently?

Well, I guess I've always been a little restless, but it hasn't really been a huge issue until recently. It really started causing serious problems when I switched into the radiologic technology training program. That was about... a year and five months ago. Before that, I could usually find ways to manage it, but now, with the expectations in the labs and classes, it's just gotten really hard to handle.

When you were in elementary school or middle school, did you have similar problems with restlessness or needing to move around? Or is this really something that's only become noticeable in the past year or so?

Yeah, it was definitely happening back then. I mean, my parents still bring up my elementary school parent-teacher conferences. They said the teachers were always complaining that I was out of my seat, or calling out answers, or just rushing ahead to do things before they even finished giving the directions. So, yeah, it was definitely an issue way before middle school, not just something that started with the radiology program.

You mentioned that in elementary school you were calling out answers and rushing ahead before the teacher finished giving directions. Do you still find yourself doing things impulsively without thinking them through first, or interrupting people when they're talking?

Yeah, I definitely still do that. It happens a lot in my training program, actually. Like, when a supervisor is explaining a positioning step for an X-ray or asking me a question, I'll just jump right in with the answer before they even finish talking. 

And then... well, then I usually realize I missed the second half of what they were saying, which is usually the part that actually mattered. It's frustrating because I'm not trying to be rude or interrupt them, the answer just sort of comes out before I can stop it.

When you think back to elementary school, would you say these problems with restlessness, interrupting, and rushing ahead were already pretty noticeable by the time you were around 11 or 12 years old?

Yeah, like I said a minute ago, it was definitely happening way before middle school. My parents still talk about those elementary school parent-teacher conferences. The teachers were always telling them that I was constantly out of my seat, calling out, or rushing ahead to do things before they even finished giving the directions. So, yeah, it was very noticeable way before I was 11 or 12. It's not just something that started with this radiology training.

Besides school and your radiology training program, have these problems with restlessness, interrupting, and rushing ahead also caused problems for you in other areas of your life — like at home with your family, or in social situations with friends?

I mean, it definitely causes some friction at home and with my friends sometimes, but honestly, the biggest problem by far is still the radiology program. It's gotten really serious there. 

My clinical evaluations have taken a huge hit lately. They actually just put me on a formal remediation plan because... well, my supervisors say my behavior disrupts the patient flow and just makes teamwork harder for everyone else. I'm really worried about it. If I don't get this under control, I'm scared it could actually cost me my place in the program.

When you were in elementary school, did these problems with restlessness, interrupting, and rushing ahead cause trouble for you at home with your parents or family members, or was it mainly just a school issue?

I'm not really sure, honestly. Um, I think it was mostly just a school thing back then. I mean, my parents probably told me to settle down or stop interrupting sometimes, but... I don't really remember it causing any major trouble at home. It was pretty much always the teachers who were the ones bringing it up and making a big deal out of it.

When you were younger, say around age 7 or 8, do you remember your parents or family members ever saying anything to you about being restless, fidgety, or interrupting them at home — or was it really just the teachers at school who were concerned about these things?

Yeah, um, like I was just saying, I really don't remember it being a big deal at home, even back when I was 7 or 8. I mean, I'm sure my parents told me to sit still at the dinner table or something, but I don't have any memories of them actually being concerned about it. It really was just the teachers who were bringing it up.

When you were around 7 or 8 years old, did your parents ever notice you having trouble sitting still or being fidgety at home — like during meals, homework time, or family activities — or is that something they never mentioned?

I really just don't recall them ever bringing it up. Like I said, I'm sure I was probably an active kid at home, but my parents never sat me down or made a point to say I was too fidgety during dinner or homework or anything like that. If they noticed it, they didn't really say anything to me about it. It was always the teachers.

When you think back to when you were very young — say, before you started school or in kindergarten — do you remember being particularly fidgety or restless compared to other kids your age, or is your earliest clear memory of these problems from around first or second grade?

I don't really remember much from before kindergarten, to be honest. My earliest clear memories of it being a problem are definitely from early elementary school. 

Like, my parents actually still talk about those elementary school parent-teacher conferences. They always bring up how the teachers said I was constantly out of my seat, calling out, or just rushing ahead before they even finished giving directions. So, yeah, it was definitely happening way back then, way before middle school, and not just something that started recently with my radiology training.
